payload.reason: The evidence supports the hypothesis that humans' robustness to noise is due to their ability to utilize general knowledge, as it contrasts with MRC models that rely solely on specific passage-question pairs.

claims.text: Humans are more robust to noise than MRC models because they can utilize general knowledge, such as inter-word semantic connections.
The integration of general knowledge into MRC models improves their robustness to noise, indicating the importance of general knowledge in reading comprehension.
The performance of the Knowledge Aided Reader (KAR) model, which uses general knowledge, is significantly better in terms of robustness to noise compared to traditional MRC models.
